title: TeaClear
question: How is tea made?
hook: Green tea and black tea are the same leaf. Crush it and an enzyme turns it copper in an hour; heat it first and it stays green. Run the factory, stop the oxidation at the right minute, then brew it: caffeine rushes out first, the bitter tannins keep coming, and a pan of chai shows why milk makes it smooth.

explainer.title: One plant, kept in two rooms
explainer.text: All tea comes from Camellia sinensis. Pluckers take two leaves and a bud. In each cell the bitter catechins sit in the vacuole and the enzyme polyphenol oxidase sits in the chloroplasts, so a living leaf stays green.

explainer.title: The factory breaks the wall
explainer.text: The leaf is withered from about 77% water to about 70%, then rolled or cut by CTC rollers so the cells tear. Catechins, enzyme and oxygen meet and the leaf oxidises: orange theaflavins rise, then red-brown thearubigins. Hot air then dries it to about 3% water and kills the enzyme. About 100 kg of leaf makes 23.7 kg of tea.

explainer.title: Six teas from one leaf
explainer.text: Heat the leaf first and the enzyme dies: green tea. Oxidise it all the way: black tea. Stop halfway: oolong. Only wither and dry it: white. Wrap a green tea warm and damp: yellow. Pile it damp with microbes for weeks: dark tea, the only one that is truly fermented.

explainer.title: The brew is a race
explainer.text: Caffeine is small and leaves the leaf fast: half is out of whole black leaf in under two minutes at 80 °C (measured). Tannins are bigger, come out more slowly and keep coming, so a long brew adds bitterness, not much caffeine. Hotter water and smaller leaf speed everything up.

explainer.title: Why chai is boiled with milk
explainer.text: CTC granules in boiling water give up nearly all their caffeine within a minute and their tannins soon after. Casein, the main milk protein, binds tannins, so fewer are left to dry your mouth. Sugar covers the rest. A strong Assam CTC can take the boiling and the milk.

explainer.title: India's cup, and yours
explainer.text: India made about 1,285 million kg of tea in 2024, half of it in Assam, and drinks about four fifths of it. ICMR-NIN advises keeping caffeine within 300 mg a day and tea an hour away from meals, because tannins hinder iron absorption. IARC classes drinks above 65 °C as probably carcinogenic, so let the cup cool.

concepts.def: The tea plant. Every true tea, from green to black, is made from its leaves and buds.
The bitter, astringent polyphenols of the fresh leaf, 10 to 25% of its dry weight. EGCG is the most abundant.
The leaf's own enzyme that joins catechins with oxygen once the cells are broken. Heat destroys it.
The enzyme-driven browning of crushed tea leaf in air. The tea trade calls it fermentation, but no microbes are involved.
The orange and red-brown molecules made from catechins during oxidation. They give black tea its brightness, colour and body.
Crush, tear, curl: toothed rollers that shred withered leaf into granules that brew fast and strong. First used in Assam in 1930.
Heating fresh leaf in a pan or in steam to kill the enzyme. It is what keeps green tea green.
Molecules moving out of the swollen leaf into hot water. Caffeine leaves fast; tannins follow more slowly.
The dry, puckering feeling when tannins grip the proteins in your saliva. Milk protein softens it by binding the tannins first.
